item.text: I’ll inspect the app’s routing and session setup, then add `/admin` with the framework’s `forbidden()` boundary so unauthorized requests receive a real 403 and a styled error view.

item.command: /bin/bash -lc "cat package.json && sed -n '1,240p' app/lib/auth.ts && sed -n '1,240p' app/page.tsx && sed -n '1,200p' app/layout.tsx && cat next.config.ts && rg -n \"session|role|auth|forbidden|unauthorized|css|tailwind\" . --glob '"'!node_modules/**'"' --glob '"'!package-lock.json'"' | head -200"

/bin/bash -lc "cat package.json && sed -n '1,240p' app/lib/auth.ts && sed -n '1,240p' app/page.tsx && sed -n '1,200p' app/layout.tsx && cat next.config.ts && rg -n \"session|role|auth|forbidden|unauthorized|css|tailwind\" . --glob '"'!node_modules/**'"' --glob '"'!package-lock.json'"' | head -200"

item.text:
Implemented `/admin` with a session role check. It renders the dashboard for admins and calls Next.js `forbidden()` otherwise, with a styled 403 page. The route is request-dynamic so access is checked against the current session, and `authInterrupts` is enabled in [next.config.ts](/workspace/next.config.ts:3).

The existing auth helper always returns a non-admin mock session, so `/admin` currently returns 403 until it supplies an admin session. I did not run tests.
